subject: an "All" category in facet_wrap or facet_gird.

messages.author: 519455d3bf64680d
messages.subject: an "All" category in facet_wrap or facet_gird.
parts:
Consider the simple graph:

ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_density(aes(x=cut))+facet_wrap(~ color, ncol
= 5) /* colour has 7 levels */

Suppose I wanted a eight graph which just depicted the overall density
function for cut, not stratified by color. I seem to recall, something
in the syntax for facet that involved "ALL", but I can't find it now,

Suggestions?

On 06/08/2010 03:57 PM, Rob James wrote:
> Consider the simple graph:
>
> ggplot(data=diamonds)+geom_density(aes(x=cut))+facet_wrap(~ color,
> ncol = 5) /* colour has 7 levels */
>
> Suppose I wanted a eight graph which just depicted the overall density
> function for cut, not stratified by color. I seem to recall,
> something in the syntax for facet that involved "ALL", but I can't
> find it now,
>
> Suggestions?
>
>

Any chance you are thinking of the margins parameter on facet_grid? I
don't think that will do what you want, though. I believe the
facet_wrap wants to work with proper subsets. The following will work
for the specific task.

diamondsall <- diamonds
diamondsall$color = factor("all")
ggplot(data=rbind(diamonds,diamondsall))
+geom_density(aes(x=cut))+facet_wrap(~ color, ncol = 5)
